ИДЕАЛЬНАЯ ИГРУЛЯ,ПУШКА ГОНКА

Аркадная мотокросс-игра, где ты не просто гоняешь по кругу, а вытворяешь сальто, супермены и прочую ерунду в воздухе, чтобы накопить нитро и потом улететь вперёд как угорелый . Самое прикольное, что управление тут заточено под простоту: не нужно заучивать сотни комбинаций, достаточно пары кнопок, чтобы скручивать трюки и чувствовать себя крутым каскадёром на городских улицах и в подземках . Графика и физика, конечно, не уровень хардкорного симулятора, но стиль такой яркий и динамичный, что грязь из-под колёс летит, а мотоцикл реально чувствуется в руках, особенно когда падаешь мордой в асфальт после неудачного прыжка . Трасс тут больше сотни, есть режим карьеры с боссами, можно прокачивать свой байк и менять прикид гонщика - в общем, залипнуть на пару вечеров можно запросто . В общем, если вы соскучились по старым добрым мотогонкам вроде Excitebike и хотите адреналина без сложных настроек - смело берите, а если вам нужен реализм и миллион настроек подвески, то лучше проходите мимо, тут всё для души.

И если этот обзор наберёт 50 лайков и 10 наград - куплю все дополнения и сыграю 100 часов. Улучшу значок до 5 уровня и схожу в церковь помолиться за разрабов, чтобы они делали только крутые проекты…

MX Nitro: Unleashed, developed by Saber Interactive and published by Mad Dog Games, LLC, is an adrenaline-fueled motocross racer that takes the traditional stunt-based racing formula and infuses it with a distinctly arcade-driven energy. It’s a game that doesn’t pretend to be a hardcore simulation of dirt bike racing—it proudly embraces exaggerated jumps, over-the-top tricks, and breakneck speed. From the very first race, the game establishes its tone: this is about showmanship as much as speed, where pulling off wild stunts in midair is just as important as crossing the finish line first. It’s the kind of experience that rewards rhythm and flow, making each successful run feel like a finely choreographed performance of danger and style.

The foundation of MX Nitro: Unleashed lies in its tight balance between control and chaos. The player begins with a modest bike and basic tricks, but as the game progresses, new moves and upgrades are unlocked that completely transform the experience. Performing flips, whips, supermans, and other high-risk tricks fuels the nitro system, which in turn allows for explosive bursts of speed. This cyclical relationship between tricks and acceleration keeps races constantly dynamic—players can’t simply rely on flawless driving; they need to combine precision with flair. The trick system itself is impressively fluid. Inputs are easy to learn but require timing and confidence to master. A well-timed stunt can shave seconds off your run, but a mistimed one can send you tumbling, forcing a restart. This balance of reward and risk keeps every jump tense and satisfying.

The level design enhances the sense of spectacle, with tracks that twist and loop through a variety of imaginative environments. From dusty desert ridges to neon-soaked cityscapes and industrial tunnels, each course feels distinct and visually engaging. The verticality of the track design is particularly effective—massive ramps and near-vertical drops emphasize the air time that the game’s trick system thrives on. Saber Interactive’s attention to the flow of the courses ensures that players rarely feel lost or frustrated; every ramp, bump, and hazard feels intentionally placed to keep the action moving at a relentless pace. The developers also included boss challenges, where rival riders serve as both obstacles and skill checks. These duels add variety to the campaign, forcing players to push the limits of their control and creativity to maintain dominance.

In terms of presentation, MX Nitro: Unleashed exudes vibrant arcade energy. The graphics may not rival modern AAA racers, but they carry a crisp and colorful aesthetic that complements the game’s tone perfectly. The particle effects during nitro boosts, the sparks from midair collisions, and the detailed animations during stunts all contribute to the visual spectacle. The sound design amplifies the intensity—engines roar, the crowd cheers, and the background music pumps with rhythmic momentum. It’s clear that the game’s intention is to keep players locked into a state of forward motion, with both visuals and audio feeding into the same exhilarating loop. The performance remains smooth even at high speeds, ensuring that the player’s reflexes, not technical hiccups, determine victory or defeat.

MX Nitro: Unleashed’s campaign mode is structured to provide a steady sense of progression. Completing races and challenges earns credits that can be used to upgrade bikes or unlock new ones, while mastering advanced tricks gradually improves your skill set. Each new area introduces more complex track designs and tougher opponents, but the learning curve feels fair. The game also introduces difficulty options, making it accessible to newcomers while still challenging experienced players who want to perfect their runs. However, the lack of multiplayer or online leaderboards somewhat limits its long-term appeal. Once the campaign is complete and the stunts have been mastered, the motivation to return diminishes. Still, the generous number of levels and optional challenges ensure several hours of engaging, high-energy gameplay.

The game’s physics strike an interesting balance between realism and exaggeration. While the handling of the bikes feels weighty enough to give jumps and landings impact, the stunts and boosts push far into arcade territory. This hybrid approach allows for both immersion and freedom; players can sense the power of their bike, yet still defy gravity in spectacular ways. Occasionally, however, the physics can feel unpredictable, especially when landing at odd angles or colliding with obstacles. These moments of inconsistency can break the rhythm of an otherwise finely tuned experience, though they rarely ruin the overall enjoyment. Saber Interactive clearly prioritized fun over authenticity, and for a game like this, that decision works in its favor.

Where MX Nitro: Unleashed shines brightest is in its flow—the satisfying loop of performing tricks, managing nitro, and maintaining control under extreme speed. Every successful jump feels earned, every perfect landing feels powerful, and every victory feels deserved. The sense of forward momentum rarely lets up, making the game easy to lose yourself in for hours at a time. Yet, its simplicity is also its limitation. Beyond the core stunt-racing mechanics, there’s little depth to discover. Customization options are minimal, and once you’ve experienced each track, there’s not much to compel continued play beyond improving your times or scores. For some, that streamlined focus will be refreshing; for others, it may feel like the game doesn’t reach its full potential.

In the end, MX Nitro: Unleashed is an unapologetically arcade-driven racing experience that celebrates the thrill of motion and the artistry of stunts. It’s fast, flashy, and accessible, designed to deliver instant bursts of excitement rather than long-term progression or realism. While it may not have the complexity or depth of major motocross simulators, it makes up for it with personality, energy, and sheer fun. The responsive controls, fluid trick system, and inventive track designs make it a memorable entry in the motocross genre. For players seeking an exhilarating, over-the-top racer that values fun over fidelity, MX Nitro: Unleashed delivers exactly what its name promises—speed, stunts, and the constant rush of nitro-fueled excitement.

EDIT: I'm editing this review because I feel like I gave it too much credit, this game still has balance issues and terrible design choices, not to mention awful DLC. It's not bad, just not great and not poor.

When it comes to gameplay, you'll like it if you're a supercross or trials fan, the gameplay is spot on, the trick system is awesome and the animations are very cool. Don't try to write this off as a trials rip off because this game does things a lot better than trials, it focuses on the pure Motocross riding and tricking, so try not to let the laid back presentation fool you. Some of the bosses you race against are pretty funny, such as the first freestyle boss. This game does have some fair share of problems that prevent this game from being perfect, first of all, this game has terrible balance issues, especially the bikes, the bike stats are horribly unbalanced across the five bikes available in this game, once I saved enough money to buy the beast bike, I never went for any of the other bikes because it obviously has the best stunts for racing, speed, and freestyle, not even the pulsar can keep up with the beast. A score attack mode would be nice so you could choose any level and go for a high score with no campaign interference or fixed props. Another problem is the trick sync events, which comes from hell itself, ♥♥♥♥, THOSE, EVENTS. Those events are extreme on frustration, and those are easily the worst things about this whole experience, the first two aren't bad, but at the later trick sync events where it involves three buttons and then a modifier for tricks with strict timing, it makes you want to toss your controller against a wall, even if you enter the right button combination quickly during a jump, the trick won't come out and you'll risk starting over, thank goodness for the quick restart feature otherwise I would have gone mad trying to complete those awful challenges. But despite those, it's a satisfactory game, if they made progression and difficulty more forgiving and fair, it would be great. Also, the DLC is can go to hell, its cool that it adds new levels and motocross gear, but the level designs are awful, unfair, and ridiculous, like the first level which starts you with no nitro and have to make a long impossible jump without enough nitro to make it, resulting in blatantly unfair play, that it makes you wish there is cheat codes because those levels are abysmal, or you just lose interest.

Get it on sale, and not on full price, because you have been warned of the games atrocious difficulty near the end of the game, and the impossible difficulty on the DLC. it's passable, just not fantastic or awful.

It's very well made for what it is and will give you an adrenaline rush if you manage to get past the learning curve. This game is much harder than most racing games because you have to know how the combo system works and memorize the level layouts. It's like a BMX racing version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater. You race along a linear path and try to do tricks to build up "nitro" which gives you a speed boost. Spinning multiplies the trick counter. If you do too many of the same tricks, then the nitro builds up slower, and I think this is the easiest place to mess up in this game.

The campaign also has you doing levels where you compete for the most points and "boss fights" which are just very hard racing sequences. As you progress you unlock better bikes and other upgrades like new tricks. The game only took me around eighth hours to beat but I had a lot of fun playing it. I would go for the achievements but they are very "checklisty"  and a lot are online only so I  decided to skip them.
Good game. If you can't get enough of trials then buy this one.

Alright, so MX Nitro Unleashed tries to capture the magic of Trials, but ends up bogging down the experience with a bunch of unnecessary fluff. It's like they took a perfectly good cake and slathered it with too much frosting. You've got a boatload of customization options, but guess what? They're all locked away in loot boxes that require more grinding than a pepper mill.

And don't even get me started on the voice-overs and cutscenes – they interrupt the game like a telemarketer during dinner. To make matters worse, the rubber-banding AI ensures that your opponents will always be breathing down your neck, no matter how well you're racing. It's like being stuck in a bad dream where you're trying to run but can't get anywhere.

Now, it's not all doom and gloom – the ultra-wide screen support and arcade racing gameplay are nice touches.. But the difficulty? It's all over the place, like a kangaroo on a pogo stick. You start off with a bike that couldn't pull the skin off a rice pudding, and it only gets easier as you upgrade. All in all, MX Nitro Unleashed is a bit of a hot mess.

"Мотокросс, заряженный Нитро, безбашеными трюками и скоростью - это MX Nitro!"

Отличная сочная картинка, драйвовый музон и безбашенные трюки в придачу. Круто? Круууто!

育碧的特技摩托也就笑笑，真要看特技就得玩这个  越野摩托：氮气
要不是最近突然想回味一下小学玩的U3D游戏，不然这么一款续作真的被尘封了，打开游戏，熟悉的音乐和玩法，瞬间就确认了

这个游戏别看才是17年出，它的前作是一款2012年的网页unity 3d游戏《motocross：nitro》(没错，比育碧的特技摩托还早)
说起这款网页U3D游戏，在8年前配置不佳的电脑上不要太良心，仅仅75mb就拥有尚可的画质，简简单单的几个按键就可以做出上十几种夸张的特技动作，加上有“氮气”这一加持，不仅有了特技难度，还拥有了速度感。自定义车辆以及人物，多达8个场景的地图，还有三种不同的比赛模式，丰富的游戏性，可谓是麻雀虽小五脏俱全。
一年后的圣诞节甚至更新了圣诞主题，多了雪橇摩托。

时隔4年后的2017年，这款新作通过新引擎的制作拥有了与育碧的特技摩托相当的画面与特效，即使是放到现在也不会觉得过时。这次的新作不仅更多的动作细节和自定义，还有更多的地图与赛程，氮气特效更加具备速度感。

总结：
+画面特效
+特技动作(真正的贴合特技摩托主题)
+丰富自定义
+完整的赛程生涯
+多样的场景地图
